notes:
Large pieces can now be sent to the second tablet.

**A big book used to fail part way through.** Sending something like a full hymnal would stop around half way and give up, and each retry got a little further from finishing. There was a 25 second limit that was meant to apply to *connecting* to the other tablet, but it was ending the transfer itself — so anything that took longer than 25 seconds to send was cut off mid-way. Small pieces always finished well inside that, which is why only large ones failed. A transfer can now take as long as it needs, and is only abandoned if it genuinely goes silent.

**The second tablet no longer gives up while the first one is still getting ready.** Sending a piece means gathering it and everything on it into a single file first, which is quick for a hymn and slow for a hymnal. The second tablet used to start its stopwatch immediately and run out of patience before the first had finished preparing. The first tablet now says **"Preparing … to send"**, and the second waits for word that the transfer is actually starting.

The progress percentage is also measured properly now, against the real size of what's being sent.

**Turning off Dual Mode with the long press now closes the second tablet's tabs**, so it isn't left holding pieces you only ever opened on the main tablet.

Your library, annotations and licence are not affected.
